pageCache.pageTitle: North Hinksey CofE Primary School 	 - Breakfast and After School Clubs
pageCache.text:
BREAKFAST CLUB AND AFTER SCHOOL CLUB
Breakfast Club runs every day from 7.30am and costs £6.50 per session.
After School Club runs every day, Monday to Thursday from 3.10 - 6.00pm (£15 per session), and Fridays 3.10 - 5.00pm (£12 per session).
Bookings for both clubs should be made through the MyChildAtSchool (MCAS) app. CLICK HERE for instructions.
We accept childcare vouchers / Tax-Free childcare payments.

pageCache.pageTitle: North Hinksey CofE Primary School 	 - Childcare Vouchers
pageCache.text:
Childcare Vouchers
We are pleased to accept childcare voucher / Tax-Free Childcare payments for any school-run after school clubs and wraparound care. We accept payments from most of the major providers.
Please note that childcare vouchers / Tax-Free Childcare can only be used to pay for approved childcare on registered premises. They cannot be used for any part of a child’s compulsory education costs, such as:
• Private lessons during school time, such as private music lessons
• School trips. If you would like to pay by childcare voucher, please book a place on each club / wraparound session through MCAS. Payment will NOT be collected through MCAS. You can then release the required funds from your childcare voucher provider / Tax-Free Childcare account to the school.
Details for payments are below. If your provider is not listed, please contact the school office for advice.

pageCache.text:
Welcome to "the sett and hive" at north Hinksey Nursery
We provide care and education for preschool children aged 9 months to 4 years old and extended day care for our nursery children between 8.00 am and 5.00 pm Monday- Thursday inclusive and 8.45am-3.15pm on Fridays.
We are are part of North Hinksey Primary School since merging from September 2025.
We are open 38 weeks each year, term time only, offering a mix of:
• Government funded free sessions - visit our News pages!
• Morning, afternoon and full daycare sessions
• Breakfast club for Nursery Children
• After-School club for Nursery children

pageCache.pageTitle: North Hinksey CofE Primary School 	 - Activity Clubs
pageCache.text:
Activity Clubs
We offer a variety of after school activity clubs for our children. Please click here for details on clubs running in the Autumn Term 2026-27 (updated July 2026).
Bookings and Payments
Bookings and payments for all clubs (except Chess and Debutots) must be made through MyChildAtSchool (MCAS).
Payment for all clubs (except Chess and Debutots) can be made with childcare vouchers. When booking on MCAS, please select the ‘Offline Payment’ option when you get to the checkout screen. Clubs run by external providers are not currently eligible for payment by childcare vouchers. Please click here for information on childcare voucher payments.
If your child is in receipt of Free School Meals, they are entitled to attend two after school activity clubs per term without charge. Please book through MCAS and select the ‘Offline Payment’ option when you get to the checkout screen. Bookings for additional clubs will be charged at the usual rate.

pageCache.pageTitle: North Hinksey CofE Primary School 	 - Curriculum
pageCache.text:
Curriculum
Children start to learn about the world around them from the moment they are born. The care and education offered in "The Sett" and "The Hive" at North Hinksey Nursery helps children to continue to do this by providing them with interesting activities that are right for their age and stage of development.We operate in the main playroom for the majority of the day with all children aged 2, 3 and 4 together. Our under 2's are in our smaller play space called "The Hive". We provide children with age/ stage appropriate support, and have some group times that enable us to differentiate activities. We have an overarching plan of where we would like the children to be, in terms of their development, for when they leave us to start school, however this is flexible, taking into account the children's starting points, familial experiences as well as thier interests. Our Curriculum is "What we intend to Teach Children" and our Pedagogy is "How we're going to Teach them". Key persons will consider the impact of this, through ongoing assessments, and keep a memory book of things the children have learnt, said and achieved, which will be shared with parents throughout their time with us.
Click here for parents guide to our Ethos, Curriculum and Pedagogy
Revised EYFS January 2024
From January 2024 there are 2 statutory EYFS frameworks:
We follow the second which can be found here. This was revised again for September 2025: Click here
The Early Years Foundation Stage curriculum (2025) sets the standards for all early years settings in the United Kingdom. “Every child deserves the best possible start in life and the support that enables them to fulfil their potential. Children develop quickly in the early years and a child’s experiences between birth and age five have a major impact on their future life chances. A secure, safe and happy childhood is important in its own right. Good parenting and high-quality early learning together provide the foundation children need to make the most of their abilities and talents as they grow up.”
EYFS statutory framework for childminders
Working together for your children
We recognise parents are the Child's first educator, and we aim to work closely with and alongside parents. Where possible we have a high ratio of adults to children in the setting. This helps us to:
• give time and attention to each child• talk with the children about their interests and activities• help children to experience and benefit from the activities we provide• allow the children to explore and be adventurous in safety

pageCache.pageTitle: North Hinksey CofE Primary School 	 - First Days
pageCache.text:
First Days
The first days
We want your child to feel happy and safe at our Nursery. To make sure that this is the case, the staff will work with you to decide on how to help your child to settle into our routines. The Nursery has a policy about helping children through transitions to school or other settings: a copy is enclosed in our policies. An annual transition plan is developed and shared with relevant parents, before the summer term.
Click HERE to view the policy on transferring records
Clothing
We provide protective clothing for the children when they play with messy activities.
We encourage children to gain the skills which help them to be independent and look after themselves. These include taking themselves to the toilet and taking off - and putting on - outdoor clothes; please consider this when choosing their clothing - in order to make their lives easier!
Mishaps can, and do happen for all sorts of reasons, especially at first. We keep a stock of spare pants, socks, jumpers, etc and are happy to lend these, but your child may prefer to keep a bag with spare items of their own clothes on their peg, to change as necessary.

pageCache.pageTitle: North Hinksey CofE Primary School 	 - Parental Involvement
pageCache.text:
Parental Involvement
How parents take part in the Nursery
Our most recent Ofsted report as North Hinksey Preschool and Childcare Clubs, prior to our merrger with North Hinksey Primary (June 2025) highlighted our parent involvement with our pre-school, saying:
" Partnerships with parents are exemplary. Parents completely value satff's support and guidance about child development and feel completely involved in their children's time at the setting".
"parents in their testimonials consistently use the the word 'thrive' to describe their children's time at preschool, attributing this to the staff team and leadership of preschool. Staff continually share children's learning so that parents can seamlessly continue this at home".
As a member of the Early Years Alliance, North Hinksey Nursery recognises parents as the first and foremost educators of their children. All of the staff see themselves as co-workers with you in providing care and education for your child. There are many ways in which parents take part in making the Nursery a welcoming and stimulating place for children and parents, such as:
• exchanging knowledge about their children's needs, activities, interests and progress with the staff• helping at sessions of the Nursery• sharing their own special interests with the children• helping to provide, make and look after the equipment and materials used in the children's play activities• taking part in events and informal discussions about the activities and curriculum provided by the Nursery• joining in community activities in which the Nursery takes part• building friendships with other parents in the Nursery

pageCache.pageTitle: North Hinksey CofE Primary School 	 - Nursery Fees
pageCache.text:
Nursery Fees
From April 1st 2025
Fees will be reviewed annually. To simplify Nursery children's drop off and collection, our extended day allows children to be dropped off at 8.45am and 3.15pm. This fee is not a condition of attendance or utilising Government Funding for Childcare places.
£42 per session (3 hours) £7 for extended day (30 minutes)
£36 per session (3 hours) £6 for extended day (30 minutes)
£30 per session (3 hours) £5 for extended day (30minutes)
Childcare Reforms From September 25
From September 2025 the government are funding more childcare and you can find out more by clicking on the above link.
Eligible working parents will be able to claim 30 hours of funding, for children from 9 months old and 2, 3 and 4 year olds from September 2025.
For Children under 2 the 30 hours of funding can be used between the hours of 8.00-5.00. (9 hours of funding)
Children aged 2-4 years the funding can be used between the hours of 9.00-3.00, (3 hours of funding).
All parents of 3 and 4 year olds can claim 15 hours of funding already, even if you are not eligilble for 30 hours.
We will be charging for a 15 minute session (early and late bird) 8.45-9.00 and 3.00-3.45 for those children attending the full day, if they are to be dropped off at 8.45 and/ or collected at 3.15.
Sessions can be booked in any combination of morning, afternoon or full day sessions where space is available.
Note, we require 6 weeks notice for cancellation of any sessions, for which fees remain payable during the period of notice.
As we are an Ofsted registered childcare provider, parents are able to apply for Working Families Tax Credits (WFTC) to help with the costs of any of our sessions. Further information is available on the Inland Revenue website.
For information about funding to to acquire the code needed visit: www.beststartinlife.gov.uk
You will need the code before you are offered a place.Please telephone the Nursery on 01865 248626 option 2 for further details or to register your child for any of our sessions and clubs.

Admissions
Admissions to North Hinksey CE Primary School are dealt with by Oxfordshire County Council. Further information can be found at: www.oxfordshire.gov.uk/primaryadmissions
​The following admissions policies provide more details about admission to North Hinksey CE Primary School when your child is due to start primary school, including the published admission number.
Admissions to join the school in other years and in-year admissions are also managed centrally by Oxfordshire County Council, please contact the Admissions Team on 01865 815175.
​If you are interested in an in-year admission and would like to visit our school prior to making an application, please contact the school office.
